title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes, where Grothendieck builds an axiomatic, combinatorial theory of 'figures'. A figure is a finite poset M of 'multistrates' ordered by a face relation ≤ (strictly <). Each X has a 'shadow' X̃, a closed set in an ambient set of 'lieux'. Its open part is X̃° = X̃ minus the union of the X̃' with X' < X. There is also a refinement relation Y ≪ X (Y is a cell of a subdivision lying over X), and F_Y denotes the subfigure {Y' ≤ Y}.

The previous page tried to define the 'carrier' map from a refinement F' to F. It sends x' to the unique X with X̃'° ⊂ X̃°. It took X minimal with X' ≪ X but could not prove the inclusion of open parts; Grothendieck wrote 'il semblerait qu'il manque quelque chose'.

This page supplies the missing ingredient as numbered item 8. Most likely it is an added condition or axiom ('Cond 8'), although the transcription reads 'Cons'.
- Setting: take Y ≪ X and a proper face X' < X.
- The induced refinement: let R_{X'} = {Y' ≤ Y : Y' ≪ X'}. This is a subfigure of F_Y refining X', called the refinement of X' induced by Y.
- The requirement: every common refinement Z of Y and X' refines some Y' in R_{X'}.
- Consequence: any figure refining both F_Y and F_{X'} refines R_{X'}. So R_{X'} is the infimum of F_Y and F_{X'} for ≪.
- In particular, Ỹ ∩ X̃' = ∪_{Y' ∈ R_{X'}} Ỹ'.

Corollary: suppose there is no X_1 with Y ≪ X_1 < X, i.e. X is minimal among cells refined by Y. Then Ỹ° ⊂ X̃°.
Proof:
1. Let x ∈ Ỹ°. Since Ỹ ⊂ X̃, x lies in X̃.
2. Suppose x ∈ X̃' for some X' < X. Then x ∈ Ỹ ∩ X̃', so x ∈ Ỹ' for some Y' ∈ R_{X'}.
3. By definition of the open part Ỹ°, this forces Y' = Y.
4. Hence Y ≪ X' < X, contradicting minimality.

The next page draws the conclusion: each open stratum of a refinement lies in a unique open stratum of the original figure. In modern terms, this is the existence of the carrier map of a subdivision.
errors: The text says Y' = [struck X]; the argument requires Y' = Y (x in the open part of Ỹ cannot lie in the shadow of a proper face Y' < Y).
That R_{X'} is a subfigure (closed under ≤) silently uses compatibility of ≪ with ≤: Y'' ≤ Y' ≪ X' should imply Y'' ≪ X' or ≪ a face of X'. This is not justified here.

Passing from 'every common refinement Z refines some Y'' to the set-theoretic equality Ỹ ∩ X̃' = ∪ Ỹ' needs every point (lieu) of the intersection to be represented by a common refinement. This presumably comes from another axiom, but it is not stated.
Condition 8 is essentially postulated to close the gap noticed on p.42 rather than derived. So the corollary's correctness depends on accepting it as an axiom.

ideas.what: Induced refinement of a face: given a subdivision Y of a cell X and a face X' of X, the cells of Y lying over X' form a subdivision of X'
ideas.modern_name: restriction of a (polyhedral/CW) subdivision to a face; induced subdivision
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (Alexander, Newman, J.H.C. Whitehead, 1920s-30s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5; the axiomatics of figures/refinements are unpublished

ideas.what: R_{X'} as the infimum (meet) of F_Y and F_{X'} for the refinement relation; Ỹ ∩ X̃' as a union of shadows of cells of R_{X'}
ideas.modern_name: common refinement / meet of subdivisions; intersection of closed cells is a subcomplex
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in polyhedral and CW complex theory

ideas.what: Each open cell of a refinement lies in the open cell of the minimal cell it refines

missed.claim: This is a step in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs' (figures, multistrates, shadows, refinements ≪). Here he isolates exactly the axiom needed to make the carrier map of a refinement well defined: the induced refinement on a face is the meet of the two figures. This documents how the axiom system of his tame-topology project was built by trial and gap-repair; it is not a new theorem.
missed.quote: Alors toute raffinement commun Z de Y et de X' raffine un des Y', i.e. raffine R_{X'}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a combinatorial foundation of 'topologie modérée'. Comparable modern frameworks are o-minimal cell decompositions and stratified/poset-indexed spaces (exit paths, Lurie's stratified homotopy theory). The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine combinatorial-topology facts (induced subdivision on faces, carrier map) formulated in Grothendieck's own unpublished axiomatics. Interesting only as documentation of how the unpublished tame-topology framework was built.
transcription_corrections: Heading 'Cons 8' is more plausibly 'Cond 8' (a numbered condition/axiom); uncertain.
Margin note reads roughly 'Restriction des raffinements induits'; uncertain.
'sous-figure R_{X'} de la multistructure ∈ F_Y' probably reads 'sous-figure R_{X'} de multistrates ∈ F_Y'.
In the last line, the intended statement is 'Y' = Y par déf. de Ỹ°' (an X is struck/overwritten); the logic requires Y' = Y.
'(c'est la situation de tantôt)' refers back to the minimal X chosen on p.42.
Corollary heading appears as 'Cor' with a struck word and an inserted 'Th[?]'; the content is a corollary of Cond 8.
